sanskrit: yuyutsur viduraś caiva saṃjayaś ca mahādyutiḥ sudharmā caiva dhaumyaś ca yathāsvaṃ jagmur ālayān
english: Yuyutsu and Vidura, and Saṃjaya of great splendor, and Sudharmā and Dhaumya too—each departed to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: saha sātyakinā śaurir arjunasya niveśanam viveśa puruṣavyāghro vyāghro giriguhām iva
english: Together with Sātyaki, Śauri, that tiger among men, entered Arjuna's dwelling, as a tiger enters a mountain cave.

sanskrit: tatra bhakṣānnapānais te samupetāḥ sukhoṣitāḥ sukhaprabuddhā rājānam upatasthur yudhiṣṭhiram
english: There, well provided with food, dishes, and drink, they rested at ease; and waking refreshed, they attended upon King Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca prāpya rājyaṃ mahātejā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yad anyad akarod vipra tan me vaktum ihārhasi
english: Janamejaya said: When the mighty-spirited Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira had won the kingdom, whatever else he did, O brāhmaṇa, that you ought now to tell me.

sanskrit: bhagavān vā hṛṣīkeśas trailokyasya paro guruḥ ṛṣe yad akarod vīras tac ca vyākhyātum arhasi
english: And whatever the blessed Hṛṣīkeśa, the supreme teacher of the three worlds, that hero, did—that too, O sage, you ought to expound.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇu rājendra tattvena kīrtyamānaṃ mayānagha vāsudevaṃ puraskṛtya yad akurvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear, O lord of kings, faultless one, as I truly recount what the Pāṇḍavas did, with Vāsudeva set before them.

sanskrit: prāpya rājyaṃ mahātejā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ cāturvarṇyaṃ yathāyogaṃ sve sve dharme nyaveśayat
english: Having won the kingdom, the mighty-spirited Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira established the four varṇas, fittingly, each in its own dharma.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasraṃ ca snātakānāṃ mahātmanām sahasraniṣkam ekaikaṃ vācayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And to a thousand great-souled brāhmaṇas who had completed their studentship, the Pāṇḍava had a thousand niṣkas of gold proclaimed for each one.

sanskrit: tathānujīvino bhṛtyān saṃśritān atithīn api kāmaiḥ saṃtarpayām āsa kṛpaṇāṃs tarkakān api
english: Likewise he satisfied with their desires his dependents, his servants, those who had taken refuge with him, and his guests, even the destitute and the petty disputants.

sanskrit: purohitāya dhaumyāya prādād ayutaśaḥ sa gāḥ dhanaṃ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca
english: To Dhaumya, his household priest, he gave cattle by the ten thousand, and wealth, gold, silver, and garments of many kinds.

sanskrit: kṛpāya ca mahārāja guruvṛttim avartata vidurāya ca dharmātmā pūjāṃ cakre yatavrataḥ
english: And toward Kṛpa, O great king, he conducted himself as toward a teacher; and that righteous one of steadfast vows did honor to Vidura.

sanskrit: bhakṣānnapānair vividhair vāsobhiḥ śayanāsanaiḥ sarvān saṃtoṣayām āsa saṃśritān dadatāṃ varaḥ
english: With food, dishes, and drink of many kinds, with garments, beds, and seats, that best of givers gladdened all who had taken refuge with him.

sanskrit: labdhapraśamanaṃ kṛtvā sa rājā rājasattama yuyutsor dhārtarāṣṭrasya pūjāṃ cakre mahāyaśāḥ
english: Having restored what had been won to peace, that king of great renown, O best of kings, did honor to Yuyutsu, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrāya tad rājyaṃ gāndhāryai vidurāya ca nivedya svasthavad rājann āste rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Having entrusted that kingdom to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, to Gāndhārī, and to Vidura, King Yudhiṣṭhira, O king, dwelt as though at ease.

sanskrit: tathā sarvaṃ sa nagaraṃ prasādya janamejaya vāsudevaṃ mahātmānam abhyagacchat kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: And having thus brought the whole city to contentment, O Janamejaya, he approached the great-souled Vāsudeva with palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: tato mahati paryaṅke maṇikāñcanabhūṣite dadarśa kṛṣṇam āsīnaṃ nīlaṃ merāv ivāmbudam
english: Then upon a great couch, adorned with jewels and gold, he beheld Kṛṣṇa seated, dark as a rain-cloud upon Meru.

sanskrit: jājvalyamānaṃ vapuṣā divyābharaṇabhūṣitam pītakauśeyasaṃvītaṃ hemnīvopahitaṃ maṇim
english: Blazing with his beauty, adorned with divine ornaments, wrapped in yellow silk—like a jewel set within gold.

sanskrit: kaustubhena uraḥsthena maṇinābhivirājitam udyatevodayaṃ śailaṃ sūryeṇāptakirīṭinam naupamyaṃ vidyate yasya triṣu lokeṣu kiṃ cana
english: Resplendent with the Kaustubha jewel resting upon his breast, like the eastern mountain crowned by the rising sun—he for whom no likeness exists anywhere in the three worlds.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ viṣṇuṃ puruṣavigraham uvāca madhurābhāṣaḥ smitapūrvam idaṃ tadā
english: Approaching that great-souled one, Viṣṇu in human form, he then, sweet of speech, spoke this with a smile.

sanskrit: sukhena te niśā kaccid vyuṣṭā buddhimatāṃ vara kaccij jñānāni sarvāṇi prasannāni tavācyuta
english: Has your night passed in comfort, O best of the wise? Are all your faculties of knowledge serene, O Acyuta?

sanskrit: tava hy āśritya tāṃ devīṃ buddhiṃ buddhimatāṃ vara vayaṃ rājyam anuprāptāḥ pṛthivī ca vaśe sthitā
english: For relying upon that divine intelligence of yours, O best of the wise, we have attained the kingdom, and the earth abides under our sway.

sanskrit: bhavatprasādād bhagavaṃs trilokagativikrama jayaḥ prāpto yaśaś cāgryaṃ na ca dharmāc cyutā vayam
english: By your grace, O blessed one whose stride ranges through the three worlds, victory has been won and foremost glory; nor have we fallen from dharma.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā bhāṣamāṇaṃ tu dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram novāca bhagavān kiṃ cid dhyānam evānvapadyata
english: But to Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, speaking thus, the blessed one said nothing at all; he passed instead into meditation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kim idaṃ paramāścaryaṃ dhyāyasy amitavikrama kaccil lokatrayasyāsya svasti lokaparāyaṇa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is this great marvel? You are meditating, O you of immeasurable valor. Is all well with these three worlds, O refuge of the worlds?

sanskrit: caturthaṃ dhyānamārgaṃ tvam ālambya puruṣottama apakrānto yato deva tena me vismitaṃ manaḥ
english: Having taken up the fourth path of meditation, O supreme Person, you have withdrawn, O god; therefore my mind is filled with wonder.

sanskrit: nigṛhīto hi vāyus te pañcakarmā śarīragaḥ indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi manasi sthāpitāni te
english: For the breath of fivefold function that moves within your body has been restrained by you, and all your senses have been set within the mind.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi manaś caiva buddhau saṃveśitāni te sarvaś caiva gaṇo deva kṣetrajñe te niveśitaḥ
english: Your senses and your mind have been gathered into the intellect, and that whole host, O god, has been merged by you into the Knower of the Field.

sanskrit: neṅganti tava romāṇi sthirā buddhis tathā manaḥ sthāṇukuḍyaśilābhūto nirīhaś cāsi mādhava
english: The hairs of your body do not stir; your intellect is steady, and so your mind. You have become as a post, a wall, a stone, motionless and free of all striving, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: yathā dīpo nivātastho niriṅgo jvalate 'cyuta tathāsi bhagavan deva niścalo dṛḍhaniścayaḥ
english: As a lamp set in a windless place burns unflickering, O Acyuta, so are you, O blessed god, unwavering and firm in resolve.

sanskrit: yadi śrotum ihārhāmi na rahasyaṃ ca te yadi chindhi me saṃśayaṃ deva prapannāyābhiyācate
english: If I am worthy here to hear it, and if it is no secret of yours, cut away my doubt, O god, for I have taken refuge in you and beseech you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kartā vikartā ca tvaṃ kṣaraṃ cākṣaraṃ ca hi anādinidhanaś cādyas tvam eva puruṣottama
english: For you are the maker and the unmaker; you are the perishable and the imperishable; you are without beginning or end, and the primordial one—you alone, O supreme Person.

sanskrit: tvatprapannāya bhaktāya śirasā praṇatāya ca dhyānasyāsya yathātattvaṃ brūhi dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: To me who have taken refuge in you, a devotee bowing with my head, tell the true nature of this meditation, O best of the upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ svagocare nyasya mano buddhīndriyāṇi ca smitapūrvam uvācedaṃ bhagavān vāsavānujaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having set his mind, intellect, and senses back upon their own objects, the blessed one, the younger brother of Vāsava, said this with a smile.

sanskrit: śaratalpagato bhīṣmaḥ śāmyann iva hutāśanaḥ māṃ dhyāti puruṣavyāghras tato me tadgataṃ manaḥ
english: Lying upon his bed of arrows, Bhīṣma, that tiger among men, like a fire sinking into stillness, meditates upon me; therefore my mind has gone toward him.

sanskrit: yasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ na sahed devarājo 'pi tam asmi manasā gataḥ
english: He whose twang of bowstring and slap of palm-guard, like the crashing of a thunderbolt, even the king of the gods could not endure—toward him have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: yenābhidrutya tarasā samastaṃ rājamaṇḍalam ūḍhās tisraḥ purā kanyās tam asmi manasā gataḥ
english: He who, charging swiftly upon the whole circle of kings, long ago carried off three maidens—toward him have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: trayoviṃśatirātraṃ yo yodhayām āsa bhārgavam na ca rāmeṇa nistīrṇas tam asmi manasā gataḥ
english: He who fought against the Bhārgava for three-and-twenty days and nights, and was not overcome by Rāma—toward him have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: yaṃ gaṅgā garbhavidhinā dhārayām āsa pārthivam vasiṣṭhaśiṣyaṃ taṃ tāta manasāsmi gato nṛpa
english: That prince whom Gaṅgā bore in her womb by ordained law, the disciple of Vasiṣṭha—toward him, my dear, toward him, O king, have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: divyāstrāṇi mahātejā yo dhārayati buddhimān sāṅgāṃś ca caturo vedāṃs tam asmi manasā gataḥ
english: That mighty-spirited, wise one who holds the divine weapons and the four Vedas with their ancillary sciences—toward him have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: rāmasya dayitaṃ śiṣyaṃ jāmadagnyasya pāṇḍava ādhāraṃ sarvavidyānāṃ tam asmi manasā gataḥ
english: The beloved disciple of Rāma the son of Jamadagni, O Pāṇḍava, the repository of all branches of knowledge—toward him have I gone in mind.

sanskrit: ekīkṛtyendriyagrāmaṃ manaḥ saṃyamya medhayā śaraṇaṃ mām upāgacchat tato me tadgataṃ manaḥ
english: Having made the whole company of his senses one, restraining his mind by his understanding, he has come to me for refuge; therefore my mind has gone toward him.

sanskrit: sa hi bhūtaṃ ca bhavyaṃ ca bhavac ca puruṣarṣabha vetti dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhas tato me tadgataṃ manaḥ
english: For he, O bull among men, knows the past, the future, and the present—that best of the upholders of dharma; therefore my mind has gone toward him.

sanskrit: tasmin hi puruṣavyāghre karmabhiḥ svair divaṃ gate bhaviṣyati mahī pārtha naṣṭacandreva śarvarī
english: For when that tiger among men has gone to heaven by his own deeds, the earth, O Pārtha, will be like a night whose moon has set.

sanskrit: tad yudhiṣṭhira gāṅgeyaṃ bhīṣmaṃ bhīmaparākramam abhigamyopasaṃgṛhya pṛccha yat te manogatam
english: Therefore, Yudhiṣṭhira, go to Bhīṣma, the son of Gaṅgā, of terrible prowess, clasp his feet, and ask whatever is in your mind.

sanskrit: cāturvedyaṃ cāturhotraṃ cāturāśramyam eva ca cāturvarṇyasya dharmaṃ ca pṛcchainaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: Ask him of the fourfold Vedic lore, of the fourfold sacrificial priesthood, of the four stages of life, and of the dharma of the four varṇas, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tasminn astamite bhīṣme kauravāṇāṃ dhuraṃdhare jñānāny alpībhaviṣyanti tasmāt tvāṃ codayāmy aham
english: When Bhīṣma, that bearer of the Kauravas' burden, has set like the sun, these branches of knowledge will grow scant; therefore I urge you on.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vāsudevasya tathyaṃ vacanam uttamam sāśrukaṇṭhaḥ sa dharmajño janārdanam uvāca ha
english: Hearing that true and excellent speech of Vāsudeva, the knower of dharma, his throat choked with tears, said this to Janārdana.

sanskrit: yad bhavān āha bhīṣmasya prabhāvaṃ prati mādhava tathā tan nātra saṃdeho vidyate mama mānada
english: What you have said concerning the power of Bhīṣma, O Mādhava, is even so; of this there is no doubt in me, O giver of honor.

sanskrit: mahābhāgyaṃ hi bhīṣmasya prabhāvaś ca mahātmanaḥ śrutaṃ mayā kathayatāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: For the great fortune of Bhīṣma and the power of that great soul have been heard by me from the lips of great-souled brāhmaṇas as they recounted them.

sanskrit: bhavāṃś ca kartā lokānāṃ yad bravīty arisūdana tathā tad anabhidhyeyaṃ vākyaṃ yādavanandana
english: And what you, the maker of the worlds, declare, O slayer of foes, that word is beyond all questioning, O joy of the Yādavas.

sanskrit: yatas tv anugrahakṛtā buddhis te mayi mādhava tvām agrataḥ puraskṛtya bhīṣmaṃ paśyāmahe vayam
english: Yet since your mind is set upon doing me grace, O Mādhava, placing you before us, we shall go to behold Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: āvṛtte bhagavaty arke sa hi lokān gamiṣyati tvaddarśanaṃ mahābāho tasmād arhati kauravaḥ
english: When the blessed sun has turned, he will depart to the other worlds; therefore, O mighty-armed one, the Kaurava deserves the sight of you.

sanskrit: tava hy ādyasya devasya kṣarasyaivākṣarasya ca darśanaṃ tasya lābhaḥ syāt tvaṃ hi brahmamayo nidhiḥ
english: For the sight of you, the primordial god, the perishable and the imperishable alike, would be his gain; for you are the treasure-house made of Brahman.

sanskrit: śrutvaitad dharmarājasya vacanaṃ madhusūdanaḥ pārśvasthaṃ sātyakiṃ prāha ratho me yujyatām iti
english: Hearing this speech of Dharmarāja, the slayer of Madhu said to Sātyaki, who stood at his side, "Let my chariot be yoked."

sanskrit: sātyakis tūpaniṣkramya keśavasya samīpataḥ dārukaṃ prāha kṛṣṇasya yujyatāṃ ratha ity uta
english: Then Sātyaki, going forth from the presence of Keśava, said to Dāruka, "Let Kṛṣṇa's chariot be yoked."

sanskrit: sa sātyaker āśu vaco niśamya; rathottamaṃ kāñcanabhūṣitāṅgam masāragalvarkamayair vibhaṅgair; vibhūṣitaṃ hemapinaddhacakram
english: Hearing at once the word of Sātyaki, he made ready the finest chariot, its body adorned with gold, embellished with facets of cat's-eye and crystal, its wheels bound with gold;

sanskrit: divākarāṃśuprabham āśugāminaṃ; vicitranānāmaṇiratnabhūṣitam navoditaṃ sūryam iva pratāpinaṃ; vicitratārkṣyadhvajinaṃ patākinam
english: radiant as the rays of the sun, swift-going, adorned with diverse and varied gems and jewels, blazing like the newly risen sun, bearing its wondrous Garuḍa-banner and its pennons;

sanskrit: sugrīvasainyapramukhair varāśvair; manojavaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitāṅgaiḥ suyuktam āvedayad acyutāya; kṛtāñjalir dāruko rājasiṃha
english: yoked well with the finest horses led by Sugrīva and Sainya, swift as thought, their bodies adorned with gold—Dāruka, with palms joined, announced it ready to Acyuta, O lion among kings.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śaratalpe śayānas tu bharatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ katham utsṛṣṭavān dehaṃ kaṃ ca yogam adhārayat
english: Janamejaya said: But lying upon his bed of arrows, the grandsire of the Bhāratas, how did he relinquish his body, and what yoga did he hold to?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājañ śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ bhīṣmasya kuruśārdūla dehotsargaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Listen attentively, O king, having become pure and composed, to the relinquishing of his body by the great-souled Bhīṣma, O tiger of the Kurus.

sanskrit: nivṛttamātre tv ayana uttare vai divākare samāveśayad ātmānam ātmany eva samāhitaḥ
english: As soon as the sun had turned upon its northern course, he, fully composed, gathered his self into the Self alone.

sanskrit: vikīrṇāṃśur ivādityo bhīṣmaḥ śaraśataiś citaḥ śiśye paramayā lakṣmyā vṛto brāhmaṇasattamaiḥ
english: Like the sun with its rays spread wide, Bhīṣma, pierced by hundreds of arrows, lay invested with surpassing splendor, surrounded by the foremost of brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: vyāsena vedaśravasā nāradena surarṣiṇā devasthānena vātsyena tathāśmakasumantunā
english: By Vyāsa renowned for Vedic lore, by Nārada the divine sage, by Devasthāna, by Vātsya, and by Aśmaka and Sumantu;

sanskrit: etaiś cānyair munigaṇair mahābhāgair mahātmabhiḥ śraddhādamapuraskārair vṛtaś candra iva grahaiḥ
english: by these and by other hosts of sages, greatly blessed and great of soul, who held faith and self-restraint foremost, he was encircled as the moon by the planets.

sanskrit: bhīṣmas tu puruṣavyāghraḥ karmaṇā manasā girā śaratalpagataḥ kṛṣṇaṃ pradadhyau prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ
english: And Bhīṣma, that tiger among men, lying upon his bed of arrows, with deed, with mind, and with speech, meditated upon Kṛṣṇa, abiding with palms joined.

sanskrit: svareṇa puṣṭanādena tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam yogeśvaraṃ padmanābhaṃ viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ jagatpatim
english: With a full-resounding voice he praised the slayer of Madhu, the lord of yoga, the lotus-naveled, Viṣṇu, the ever-victorious, the lord of the world.

sanskrit: kṛtāñjaliḥ śucir bhūtvā vāgvidāṃ pravaraḥ prabhum bhīṣmaḥ paramadharmātmā vāsudevam athāstuvat
english: With palms joined, having become pure, that foremost of those skilled in speech, Bhīṣma, supremely righteous of soul, then hymned the Lord Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: ārirādhayiṣuḥ kṛṣṇaṃ vācaṃ jigamiṣāmi yām tayā vyāsasamāsinyā prīyatāṃ puruṣottamaḥ
english: "The speech I would set forth, seeking to propitiate Kṛṣṇa—by that speech, both expansive and concise, may the supreme Person be pleased.

sanskrit: śuciḥ śuciṣadaṃ haṃsaṃ tatparaḥ parameṣṭhinam yuktvā sarvātmanātmānaṃ taṃ prapadye prajāpatim
english: Pure, intent upon him, having yoked my whole self with all my being, I take refuge in that Lord of creatures, the Swan who dwells in purity, the supreme one set on high.

sanskrit: yasmin viśvāni bhūtāni tiṣṭhanti ca viśanti ca guṇabhūtāni bhūteśe sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
english: In whom all beings abide and into whom they enter, become his qualities, within the Lord of beings, as beads of gems upon a thread.

sanskrit: yasmin nitye tate tantau dṛḍhe srag iva tiṣṭhati sadasadgrathitaṃ viśvaṃ viśvāṅge viśvakarmaṇi
english: On whom, the eternal, outstretched, firm thread, the universe rests like a garland—the All, woven of being and non-being, upon him whose limbs are all things, the maker of all.

sanskrit: hariṃ sahasraśirasaṃ sahasracaraṇekṣaṇam prāhur nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ yaṃ viśvasya parāyaṇam
english: Whom they call Hari, thousand-headed, with a thousand feet and eyes, the god Nārāyaṇa, the supreme refuge of the universe.

sanskrit: aṇīyasām aṇīyāṃsaṃ sthaviṣṭhaṃ ca sthavīyasām garīyasāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca śreyasām api
english: The subtlest of the subtle, the most massive of the massive, the weightiest of the weighty, and the best even of the good.

sanskrit: yaṃ vākeṣv anuvākeṣu niṣatsūpaniṣatsu ca gṛṇanti satyakarmāṇaṃ satyaṃ satyeṣu sāmasu
english: Whom in the hymns and the recitations, in the sittings and the secret teachings, they extol as the doer of true deeds, the Truth among the true Sāman chants.

sanskrit: caturbhiś caturātmānaṃ sattvasthaṃ sātvatāṃ patim yaṃ divyair devam arcanti guhyaiḥ paramanāmabhiḥ
english: The fourfold one in his four forms, abiding in goodness, the lord of the Sātvatas, whom they worship as god with divine and secret supreme names.

sanskrit: yaṃ devaṃ devakī devī vasudevād ajījanat bhaumasya brahmaṇo guptyai dīptam agnim ivāraṇiḥ
english: The god whom the goddess Devakī brought forth from Vāsudeva, for the safeguarding of the earthly Veda, as the firestick brings forth blazing fire.

sanskrit: yam ananyo vyapetāśīr ātmānaṃ vītakalmaṣam iṣṭvānantyāya govindaṃ paśyaty ātmany avasthitam
english: Whom the undistracted one, free of all craving, having worshipped Govinda for the sake of the infinite, beholds as the self, stainless, dwelling within his own self.

sanskrit: purāṇe puruṣaḥ prokto brahmā prokto yugādiṣu kṣaye saṃkarṣaṇaḥ proktas tam upāsyam upāsmahe
english: In ancient lore he is proclaimed the Person; at the beginnings of the ages he is proclaimed Brahmā; at the dissolution he is proclaimed Saṃkarṣaṇa—him, worthy of worship, we worship.

sanskrit: ativāyvindrakarmāṇam atisūryāgnitejasam atibuddhīndriyātmānaṃ taṃ prapadye prajāpatim
english: Whose action surpasses Vāyu's and Indra's, whose splendor surpasses the sun's and fire's, whose self surpasses intellect and the senses—in him, the Lord of creatures, I take refuge.

sanskrit: yaṃ vai viśvasya kartāraṃ jagatas tasthuṣāṃ patim vadanti jagato 'dhyakṣam akṣaraṃ paramaṃ padam
english: Whom indeed they call the maker of all, the lord of the world both moving and unmoving, the overseer of the universe, the imperishable, the supreme abode.
